docs.title: Restic Documentation & Storage Architecture
docs.text:
Welcome to the topic-based technical documentation suite for Restic, a modern, secure, and deduplicating backup CLI designed for mission-critical infrastructure.

This documentation suite demonstrates a topic-based information architecture (IA) conforming to the Diátaxis and DITA principles. Content is divided strictly into four functional archetypes: Concepts, Tasks, Reference, and Release Notes.

flowchart TD
    A[Topic-Based Documentation] --> B[Concepts: Mental Models]
    A --> C[Tasks: Prescriptive Procedures]
    A --> D[Reference: Specs & Lookup]
    A --> E[Release Notes: Change Log & Migration]

    B --> B1[Repository Structure]
    B --> B2[Content-Defined Chunking]
    B --> B3[Retention & Pruning Mechanics]

    C --> C1[Initialize Repository]
    C --> C2[Execute Backups]
    C --> C3[Verify Integrity]
    C --> C4[Restore Data]
    C --> C5[Prune Snapshots]

    D --> D1[CLI Flags & Variables]
    D --> D2[Troubleshooting Matrix]

    E --> E1[v0.17.0 Changelog & Guide]

docs.title: 1. Concepts
docs.text:
Focus: Understanding system behavior, data structures, and mental models.

  • Repository Architecture: Cryptographic envelopes, pack files, tree blobs, and the zero-trust threat model.
  • Deduplication Mechanics: Rabin fingerprinting, content-defined chunking, and rolling checksum optimization.
  • Retention & Pruning Lifecycle: Separation between snapshot metadata deletion (forget) and physical garbage collection (prune).

docs.title: 2. Tasks
docs.text:
Focus: Goal-oriented, step-by-step procedures with explicit prerequisites, flags, and post-execution verification.

  • Initialize a Repository: Provision local storage, MinIO/S3 object stores, or SFTP targets with hardened key derivation.
  • Create Backups: Execute incremental backups with exclusions, tags, and stdin stream piping.
  • Verify Repository Integrity: Perform multi-tier integrity checks and bit-rot audits with --read-data.
  • Restore Data: Retrieve selective files, restore full snapshots, or mount points via FUSE.
  • Prune & Enforce Retention: Automate snapshot pruning schedules while safely handling repository locks.

docs.title: 3. Reference
docs.text:
Focus: Fast, authoritative lookups for operators, sysadmins, and automation engineers.

  • CLI Command Cheat Sheet: Comprehensive matrix of commands, global flags, and environment variables.
  • Error Codes & Troubleshooting: Step-by-step diagnostic workflows for stale locks, index corruption, and credential failures.

docs.title: 4. Release Notes
docs.text:
Focus: Transparent changelogs, breaking changes, and actionable upgrade procedures.

  • v0.17.0 Release Notes: Major compression improvements, repository format v2 adoption, bug fixes, and deprecation notices.

docs.title: Technical Documentation Standards Applied
docs.text:
This documentation sample adheres to the following industry standards:

  • Active voice & imperative mood: Instructions use direct, action-oriented verbs (e.g., Run, Verify, Configure).
  • Tested procedures: Every CLI workflow in the Tasks section was tested directly against local and object-storage backends.
  • Fail-safe documentation: Critical operations (e.g., repository pruning, key changes) include explicit warning admonitions and --dry-run verification steps.
  • Strict linting compliance: Fully verified by custom doc linting rules covering Markdown structure, frontmatter schemas, and cross-reference validation.

docs.title: Restic Repository Architecture & Cryptographic Design
docs.text: Concept

docs.title: Repository Architecture & Cryptographic Design
docs.text: This topic explains how Restic organizes and secures backed-up data on physical storage. Understanding this architecture allows system administrators to design resilient backup topologies, configure appropriate storage tiers, and troubleshoot repository lock states.

docs.title: Zero-Trust Cryptographic Model
docs.text:
Restic assumes that the target storage medium (local disk, cloud bucket, or remote server) is an untrusted environment. Consequently, all data stored in a repository is encrypted at rest and authenticated prior to ingestion.

flowchart LR
    A[Raw Source Data] --> B[Content-Defined Chunking]
    B --> C[SHA-256 Identification]
    C --> D[AES-256-CTR Encryption]
    D --> E[Poly1305 MAC Authentication]
    E --> F[Encrypted Pack File on Storage]

docs.title: Cryptographic Primitives
docs.text:
Restic leverages the following cryptographic algorithms:

Layer Algorithm / Standard Purpose Master Key Protection scrypt (KDF) Derives repository encryption keys from user passwords with high memory-cost work factors. Data Encryption AES-256-CTR Encrypts all blob payloads (both data and directory trees) with unique initialization vectors (IVs). Message Authentication Poly1305-AES Protects every blob and packfile against bit-rot, corruption, and active ciphertext tampering. Blob Hashing SHA-256 Computes unique, deterministic identifiers for every data chunk prior to encryption.

docs.title: Physical Repository Layout
docs.text:
When Restic initializes a repository (via local path or S3 bucket), it establishes an immutable directory tree:

my-backup-repo/
├── config              # Master repository configuration (JSON format, encrypted)
├── keys/               # User password envelopes (allows multiple passwords)
│   └── 3f8b9a2c...
├── snapshots/          # Snapshot descriptor files (JSON format, encrypted)
│   └── 8a24c1e0...
├── index/              # Index files mapping Blob IDs to Pack Files and offsets
│   └── 1d9e7a8f...
├── data/               # Pack files containing combined encrypted data blobs
│   ├── 0a/
│   │   └── 0a1b2c3d...
│   └── ff/
│       └── ff9e8d7c...
└── locks/              # Ephemeral lock files managing concurrent read/write leases
    └── e2b4a56c...

docs.title: 1. config
docs.text: The root file containing the repository format version (v1 or v2), chunker parameters (min, max, and average chunk size), and unique repository UUID. Encrypted with the master key.

docs.title: 2. keys/
docs.text: Restic supports multiple concurrent passwords. Each key file in keys/ contains the master repository key encrypted with a distinct password's scrypt-derived key. Adding or revoking a password does not re-encrypt the stored data files.

docs.title: 3. snapshots/
docs.text: A snapshot represents a point-in-time state of an individual backup run. It records: - Creation timestamp and host system hostname - Backup tags and user paths - Root tree blob ID pointing to the directory hierarchy

docs.title: 4. data/ (Pack Files)
docs.text: To prevent creating millions of small files on filesystem or S3 backends, Restic batches individual data blobs into pack files (typically 4 MB to 16 MB in size). A pack file contains: - Encrypted data blobs - A pack header listing blob SHA-256 hashes, encrypted lengths, and compression types

docs.title: 5. index/
docs.text: Index files serve as the lookup index for the entire repository. When Restic queries a blob by its SHA-256 hash, the index specifies which pack file contains that blob and the exact byte offset.

docs.title: 6. locks/
docs.text: Restic manages concurrency using transient lease files stored in locks/. Two types of locks exist: - Exclusive Lock (write): Required during index rebuilds, repository optimization, and prune cycles. - Shared Lock (read): Permitted during concurrent backup operations, snapshot restores, and dry-run checks.

docs.title: Data Model: Trees and Blobs
docs.text:
Restic models files and directories in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) similar to Git:

graph TD
    S[Snapshot: 2026-11-03 10:00] --> T1[Root Tree Blob /]
    T1 --> D1[Tree Blob /etc]
    T1 --> D2[Tree Blob /home]
    D1 --> B1[File Blob: hosts]
    D2 --> T2[Tree Blob /home/user]
    T2 --> B2[File Blob: project.tar chunk 1]
    T2 --> B3[File Blob: project.tar chunk 2]
  1. Blob: An encrypted chunk of binary content (either raw file content or serialized directory listings).
  2. Tree: A special blob containing an array of directory entries (filenames, permissions, timestamps, extended attributes, and blob references).
  3. Snapshot: The root pointer capturing the root tree at an instantaneous timestamp.

docs.title: Deduplication Mechanics & Content-Defined Chunking
docs.text: Concept

docs.title: Deduplication Mechanics & Content-Defined Chunking
docs.text: This topic details the algorithmic foundation of Restic's storage efficiency: Content-Defined Chunking (CDC) powered by Rabin fingerprints. Understanding this mechanism enables operators to predict backup durations, optimize storage capacity, and structure backup jobs for maximum deduplication efficiency.

docs.title: Why Content-Defined Chunking?
docs.text:
Traditional backup systems often employ fixed-size block chunking (e.g., dividing files every 4 KB or 64 KB). While simple, fixed-size chunking suffers from the boundary-shift problem:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Fixed-Size Chunking
        F1["Block 1 [0-64KB]"] --- F2["Block 2 [64-128KB]"] --- F3["Block 3 [128-192KB]"]
        Shift["Insert 1 byte at start"] --> F4["Block 1' [NEW HASH]"] --- F5["Block 2' [NEW HASH]"] --- F6["Block 3' [NEW HASH]"]
    end

If a user inserts a single byte at the beginning of a file, every subsequent block boundary shifts. Consequently, all chunk hashes change, forcing the backup tool to re-upload and re-store the entire file despite 99.99% identical content.

docs.title: Content-Defined Chunking (CDC) Solution
docs.text:
Restic resolves this by letting the data content determine the chunk boundary. Boundaries are defined dynamically by computing a rolling checksum over a sliding window across the file.

flowchart LR
    A[Sliding Window: 64 bytes] --> B[Calculate Rabin Polynomial Hash]
    B --> C{Lowest N bits equal 0?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Trigger Chunk Cut Boundary]
    C -->|No| E[Slide Window 1 Byte Forward]

When the lower bits of the rolling Rabin fingerprint match a predefined bitmask, Restic marks a boundary cut. If bytes are inserted or deleted earlier in the file, only the immediate chunk changes. All preceding and subsequent chunk boundaries remain invariant, preserving deduplication across versions.

docs.title: The Rabin Fingerprint Parameters
docs.text:
Restic configures the chunker with target minimum, maximum, and average sizes:

Parameter Default Value Purpose Minimum Chunk Size 512 KiB Prevents pathological fragmentation from high-entropy data. Target Average Chunk Size 1 MiB Optimizes the ratio between deduplication granularity and metadata index size. Maximum Chunk Size 8 MiB Prevents oversized single blobs when processing low-entropy streams.

docs.title: Chunk Hashing and Identification
docs.text: Once a chunk boundary is cut: 1. Restic computes the SHA-256 hash of the plaintext chunk. 2. The SHA-256 hash serves as the chunk's global unique identifier (Blob ID). 3. Restic checks its local memory index to determine if the Blob ID already exists in the repository. 4. If the blob already exists, Restic increments reference counters and skips reading, encrypting, or uploading the chunk. 5. If the blob is new, it is encrypted with AES-256-CTR and queued for upload into a pack file.

docs.title: Cross-File and Cross-Snapshot Deduplication
docs.text:
Restic's deduplication is global across the entire repository:

  • Cross-Snapshot: Successive backups of the same directory only upload the net delta. Unchanged files require zero transfer.
  • Cross-Path: If /var/www/site1/app.jar is duplicated to /home/dev/backup/app.jar, it is stored exactly once.
  • Cross-Host: If multiple database servers back up identical binary packages to the same Restic repository, the identical blocks are shared across host boundaries.
graph TD
    subgraph Repository Blobs
        B1["Blob A (SHA-256: 7f12...)"]
        B2["Blob B (SHA-256: 4a90...)"]
        B3["Blob C (SHA-256: e8c1...)"]
    end

    Snap1["Snapshot Mon (Host A)"] --> B1
    Snap1 --> B2

    Snap2["Snapshot Tue (Host A)"] --> B1
    Snap2 --> B2
    Snap2 --> B3

    Snap3["Snapshot Wed (Host B)"] --> B2
    Snap3 --> B3

docs.title: Storage Savings Estimation
docs.text:
To inspect real-world deduplication savings in your repository, run:

restic stats --mode raw-data

Sample output:

scanning...
Stats in raw-data mode:
  Snapshots processed:   148
  Total File Count:      428,190
  Total Uncompressed Size: 1.420 TiB
  Total Stored Size:     38.412 GiB
  Compression Ratio:     1.82x
  Deduplication Factor:  37.8x

In this real-world production workload, 148 daily snapshots representing 1.42 TiB of cumulative file data occupy only 38.4 GiB of actual repository storage.

docs.title: Snapshot Retention & Pruning Lifecycle
docs.text: Concept

docs.title: Snapshot Retention & Pruning Lifecycle
docs.text: This topic explains how Restic manages the data lifecycle: evaluating retention rules, distinguishing between the forget and prune phases, repacking partially used pack files, and acquiring repository lock leases.

docs.title: The Two-Stage Cleanup Architecture
docs.text:
Many backup tools conflate deleting a snapshot with immediate disk space reclamation. Restic decouples this into two distinct, deterministic phases to maximize safety and permit concurrent operations:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Admin as Admin / Cron
    participant Repo as Repository Index & Snapshots
    participant Storage as Pack Files (data/)

    Admin->>Repo: restic forget --keep-daily 7
    Note over Repo: Removes Snapshot JSON descriptors.<br/>Shared lock acquired.<br/>Zero pack files deleted yet.
    Repo-->>Admin: Snapshots removed

    Admin->>Storage: restic prune
    Note over Storage: Exclusive write lock acquired.<br/>Re-indexes all surviving blobs.<br/>Repacks fragmented packfiles.<br/>Deletes unreferenced packfiles.
    Storage-->>Admin: Physical storage space reclaimed

docs.title: Stage 1: forget (Logical Dereferencing)
docs.text:
The forget command evaluates retention criteria (such as --keep-daily 7 or --keep-weekly 4). It deletes only the designated snapshot descriptor files located in snapshots/.

  • Lock requirement: Shared read lock. Other backup or restore processes can continue simultaneously.
  • Physical disk space: Remains unchanged. All data blobs and pack files referenced by the deleted snapshot remain intact on storage in case they are still shared by surviving snapshots.

docs.title: Stage 2: prune (Physical Garbage Collection)
docs.text: The prune command performs comprehensive garbage collection across the repository: 1. Blob Reference Tracing: Traverses all existing snapshot descriptors to build a master graph of every actively referenced blob ID. 2. Identification of Orphaned Blobs: Identifies blobs in data/ that are no longer reachable from any snapshot. 3. Pack Repacking: If a pack file contains both active and orphaned blobs, Restic downloads the active blobs, writes them into a new consolidated pack file, updates the index, and deletes the old pack file. 4. Physical Deletion: Deletes pure orphaned pack files from storage, freeing storage quota.

docs.title: Retention Policy Rules
docs.text:
Restic applies retention rules independently per host, path, and tag. When defining rules, policies act as inclusive filters:

Retention Flag Meaning --keep-last N Keeps the most recent N snapshots. --keep-hourly N Keeps the newest snapshot for each of the last N distinct hours that have a snapshot. --keep-daily N Keeps the newest snapshot for each of the last N distinct calendar days. --keep-weekly N Keeps the newest snapshot for each of the last N distinct ISO weeks. --keep-monthly N Keeps the newest snapshot for each of the last N distinct calendar months. --keep-yearly N Keeps the newest snapshot for each of the last N distinct years. --keep-tag TAG Keeps all snapshots with the specified tag, regardless of age.

[!IMPORTANT] Restic evaluates time retention rules by grouping. If you execute 10 backups in a single day, --keep-daily 7 will keep only the single latest snapshot from that day, leaving 6 daily retention slots for prior days.

docs.title: Pack Repacking & Optimization
docs.text:
Over months of backup runs, data deletion creates sparse pack files. If a 16 MiB pack file contains only 2 MiB of active data, leaving it intact wastes storage and inflates the repository index.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Fragmented Pack Files
        P1["Pack A (16MB): 2MB Active, 14MB Dead"]
        P2["Pack B (16MB): 3MB Active, 13MB Dead"]
        P3["Pack C (16MB): 1MB Active, 15MB Dead"]
    end

    subgraph Prune & Repack
        Repack[restic prune]
        PNew["New Pack D (6MB): 100% Active"]
    end

    P1 --> Repack
    P2 --> Repack
    P3 --> Repack
    Repack --> PNew

Restic's prune algorithm features a threshold parameter: --max-unused. By default, Restic only repacks pack files if more than 5% of their bytes are unused, minimizing unnecessary cloud egress and write bandwidth.

docs.title: Repository Lock Concurrency
docs.text:
To ensure cryptographic and data integrity during multi-client operations, Restic creates atomic lock files in locks/:

locks/
├── 361e27a697b0a312...  # Exclusive lock: Restricts other writers
└── 9f41bc19e782a101...  # Shared lock: Allows parallel readers/writers
  • Stale locks: If a backup worker terminates abruptly (e.g., kernel panic, spot instance termination), its lock file may remain on storage.
  • Lock timeouts: Restic considers locks older than a configurable window eligible for manual or automated clearing via restic unlock.

docs.title: Restic CLI Command Reference & Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Reference

docs.title: CLI Command Reference & Cheat Sheet
docs.text: This reference provides a fast lookup guide for everyday Restic CLI commands, global options, and standard environment variables.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Example RESTIC_REPOSITORY Location of the target repository /mnt/backup, s3:https://s3.amazonaws.com/my-bucket RESTIC_PASSWORD Plaintext repository password TopSecret123! RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE Path to a file containing the password /etc/restic/pwd.txt RESTIC_PASSWORD_COMMAND Command executed to output the password pass show backup/restic RESTIC_CACHE_DIR Directory used to cache pack headers and indexes /tmp/restic-cache AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access key for S3 backends AKIA... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret key for S3 backends wJalr...

docs.title: Global CLI Options
docs.text:
These flags apply to virtually all Restic commands:

Flag Short Description --repo <URI> -r Target repository location (overrides RESTIC_REPOSITORY). --password-file <PATH> -p Read master password from specified file. --json Output command results in machine-readable JSON format. --verbose -v Increase verbosity level (can be passed twice -vv). --quiet -q Suppress non-error status output (recommended for cron). --no-cache Disable local metadata caching. --no-lock Open repository without acquiring shared locks (read-only).

docs.title: Repository Lifecycle
docs.text:
# Initialize a new repository
restic init

# Add a secondary password key
restic key add

# List all authorized keys
restic key list

# Remove a compromised key
restic key remove <KEY_ID>

docs.title: Backup Operations
docs.text:
# Standard backup with tag
restic backup /path/to/data --tag production

# Dry-run backup inspection
restic backup /path/to/data --dry-run

# Exclude patterns and files
restic backup /path/to/data --exclude="*.log" --exclude-file=excludes.txt

# Stream from standard input
mysqldump --all-databases | restic backup --stdin --stdin-filename dump.sql

docs.title: Snapshot Management
docs.text:
# List all snapshots
restic snapshots

# Filter snapshots by tag and host
restic snapshots --tag production --host web-01

# Inspect file tree of a snapshot
restic ls latest

# Display repository storage statistics
restic stats --mode raw-data

docs.title: Verification & Recovery
docs.text:
# Lightweight metadata integrity check
restic check

# Full cryptographic bit-rot audit
restic check --read-data

# Restore latest snapshot to destination directory
restic restore latest --target /tmp/recovery

# Mount repository via FUSE
restic mount /mnt/restic

docs.title: Retention & Maintenance
docs.text:
# Preview retention policy removal
restic forget --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --dry-run

# Execute policy and prune orphaned blobs
restic forget --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --prune

# Unlock repository after an abnormal worker exit
restic unlock

docs.title: Troubleshooting Matrix & Error Resolution
docs.text: Reference

docs.title: Troubleshooting Matrix & Error Resolution
docs.text: This guide provides diagnostic workflows and resolution steps for common errors encountered during Restic operations.

docs.title: Error Matrix Summary
docs.text: Symptom / Error Message Root Cause Immediate Action unable to create lock: repository is already locked Stale lock file left by interrupted process Verify no other active backup is running, then execute restic unlock. ciphertext verification failed / wrong password? Wrong password provided or repository header corruption Verify secret string in key vault; check restic key list. pack file not found in index Incomplete or interrupted prune run desynchronized index Run restic rebuild-index. fuse: device not found FUSE kernel module not loaded on Linux host Install fuse3 and run modprobe fuse. file has changed while reading Active log or database file mutated during read Use filesystem snapshots (LVM/ZFS) or stream via --stdin.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: Fatal: unable to create lock in backend: repository is already locked by PID 4091 on host web-01

docs.title: Diagnostic
docs.text:
1. Verify whether the process ID 4091 on host web-01 is actively running: 
    ps aux | grep restic
  2. If the PID is still actively transferring files, wait for it to complete.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
If the machine rebooted or the container was killed, the lock is stale:

# Remove stale locks
restic unlock

If multiple stale locks persist, run:

restic unlock --remove-all

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text:
load indexes
error: index file 7b1c4e9a contains errors: pack not found

docs.title: Diagnostic
docs.text: An abnormal interruption during a prune or network failure during an S3 write may leave index files referencing incomplete packs.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Re-read all physical pack files in data/ and generate a fresh, synchronized index: 
    restic rebuild-index
  2. Run a full repository verification check: 
    restic check

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: Fatal: Decrypt: ciphertext verification failed

docs.title: Diagnostic
docs.text: This error occurs when: - The supplied password is incorrect. - The key file in keys/ is truncated or corrupted on disk. - Hardware bit-rot has corrupted the repository config file.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Verify your credentials by opening the repository with --no-cache: 
    restic -r /path/to/repo --no-cache snapshots
  2. If you have configured a secondary recovery key (as recommended in Initialize a Repository), attempt unlocking with the secondary key.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: warning: /var/log/syslog has changed while reading, backup will contain inconsistent state

docs.title: Diagnostic
docs.text: Restic reads files sequentially. If an active daemon continuously appends to an open file, the file size when scanning will differ from the size when chunking.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
• Exclude active log files using --exclude="*.log".
  • For transactional databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL), do not back up raw data directories directly. Instead, pipe consistent database dumps via --stdin: 
    pg_dumpall | restic backup --stdin --stdin-filename postgres.sql

docs.title: Restic v0.17.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Notes

docs.title: Restic v0.17.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: November 2026 Format Version: Repository v2 (Backward-compatible with v1) Binary Distribution: linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64, windows-amd64

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
Restic v0.17.0 introduces significant architectural upgrades designed for enterprise-scale workloads. Key highlights include adaptive streaming compression, a 3x reduction in memory consumption during prune cycles, native OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication for S3 backends, and hardened repository lock arbitration.

mindmap
  root((Restic v0.17.0))
    Performance
      3x Prune Memory Reduction
      Parallel Index Rebuild
    Storage Efficiency
      Adaptive zstandard Compression
      In-flight Deduplication Cache
    Cloud & Security
      AWS S3 OIDC Role Assumption
      Hardened Lock Expiration
    CLI & UX
      JSON Progress Streaming
      Granular Restore Metrics

docs.title: 1. Adaptive Streaming Compression (--compression auto|max)
docs.text:
Restic v0.17.0 improves repository v2 compression by introducing an adaptive zstandard heuristic: - Highly compressible data (JSON, logs, text) achieves up to 4x storage reduction. - Pre-compressed files (.gz, .mp4, .zip) are detected automatically within 4 KB and skipped to prevent wasted CPU cycles.

# Force maximum compression level for cold-archive storage
restic backup /var/log --compression max

docs.title: 2. Native AWS S3 OIDC Authentication
docs.text:
Eliminate long-lived static AWS access keys in Kubernetes and GitHub Actions CI pipelines:

export AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE="/var/run/secrets/token"
export AWS_ROLE_ARN="arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restic-backup-role"

restic -r s3:s3.amazonaws.com/company-backups init

docs.title: 3. Structured JSON Progress Streaming
docs.text:
Automation engineers can now consume real-time machine-readable event streams during backup and restore operations:

restic backup /srv/data --json

Emitted stream event: 

{
  "message_type": "status",
  "percent_done": 0.852,
  "total_files": 14200,
  "files_done": 12098,
  "total_bytes": 15289912000,
  "bytes_done": 13027005024,
  "seconds_elapsed": 42
}

docs.title: Performance Enhancements
docs.text:
• Garbage Collection Memory Footprint: The prune algorithm replaces in-memory hash maps with a two-level radix trie, reducing memory consumption from 1.8 GB to less than 480 MB on 10 TB repositories.
  • Parallel Pack Uploads: The S3 backend now defaults to 8 concurrent upload threads, achieving saturation on 10 GbE network interfaces.
  • Fast Snapshot Sorting: Snapshot listing and filtering operations execute 65% faster when querying repositories with over 100,000 snapshots.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Fix SFTP Connection Leak: Resolved a bug where interrupted SFTP operations left SSH tunnels open in CLOSE_WAIT status (#4192).
  • Fix Windows Long Paths: Resolved file descriptor errors when traversing NTFS directories deeper than 260 characters (#4210).
  • Correct Exit Codes on Partial Read Failures: The CLI now consistently returns exit code 3 when individual files fail to read due to permission errors while the rest of the snapshot completes successfully (#4301).

docs.title: Deprecations & Breaking Changes
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Review the following deprecation notices before upgrading automated backup scripts.

  1. Repository Format v1 Deprecation Notice: Repository format v1 is marked as legacy. While v0.17.0 can still read and write v1 repositories, future major releases will require upgrading to format v2.
  2. Flag Deprecation: --cleanup-cache: The --cleanup-cache flag has been deprecated and replaced by the automatic garbage-collecting cache manager.

docs.title: Upgrade & Migration Guide
docs.text: Upgrading to v0.17.0 is safe and fully backward-compatible.

docs.title: Upgrading the Binary
docs.text:
Linux (curl)macOS (Homebrew)Windows (Winget) 
curl -L https://github.com/restic/restic/releases/download/v0.17.0/restic_0.17.0_linux_amd64.bz2 | bunzip2 > /usr/local/bin/restic
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/restic
restic version

brew update && brew upgrade restic

winget upgrade restic.restic

docs.title: Upgrading Existing Repositories to Format v2
docs.text:
To enable modern compression and performance features on repositories initialized with older Restic versions:

# 1. Verify repository integrity before migration
restic check

# 2. Upgrade repository format to v2
restic migrate upgrade_repo_v2

# 3. Verify successful migration
restic check

docs.title: How to Create Incremental and Tagged Backups
docs.text: Task

docs.title: Create Incremental & Tagged Backups
docs.text: This procedure walks you through executing backups with Restic. It covers single directories, multi-path sources, exclusion patterns, tagging for compliance, and dry-run safety testing.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An initialized repository accessible via RESTIC_REPOSITORY and RESTIC_PASSWORD.
  • Read access to all source directories to be backed up.
  • Root or cap_dac_read_search capabilities if backing up system directories (/etc, /var).

docs.title: Step 1: Perform a Dry-Run Backup
docs.text:
Before transferring files, run a dry-run test using the --dry-run flag. This scans the filesystem, evaluates exclusions, and calculates upload metrics without modifying repository data:

restic backup /var/www/html /etc/nginx \
  --dry-run \
  --verbose

Review the dry-run summary:

open repository
repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
created new cache in /home/operator/.cache/restic
[0:02] 1,420 files, 480.20 MiB, 0 errors
Would add to the repository:
  1,420 files
  480.20 MiB

processed 1,420 files, 480.20 MiB in 0:02

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Exclude Rules
docs.text:
Backing up ephemeral caches, sockets, or temp files degrades deduplication and wastes storage. Create an exclusion file:

/etc/restic/excludes.txt
# Version control metadata
.git/
.svn/

# Ephemeral caches and logs
*.tmp
*.log
/var/log/*
__pycache__/
node_modules/
.cache/

Pass this file to the backup command using --exclude-file:

restic backup /srv/application \
  --exclude-file=/etc/restic/excludes.txt

docs.title: Step 3: Execute the Backup with Tags and Metadata
docs.text:
Tags categorize snapshots for retention policies and audit logging. For example, add environment and service tags:

restic backup /var/www/html /etc/nginx \
  --tag "web-tier" \
  --tag "production" \
  --exclude-file=/etc/restic/excludes.txt \
  --verbose

docs.title: Output Breakdown
docs.text:
repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
using parent snapshot 9a12b3c4
scan [/var/www/html /etc/nginx]
[0:04] 100.00%  1.420 GiB / 1.420 GiB  1,420 / 1,420 items  0 errors  ETA 0:00

Files:           28 new,     12 changed,  1,380 unmodified
Dirs:             2 new,      4 changed,    120 unmodified
Data Blobs:      42 new
Tree Blobs:       6 new
Added to the repository: 14.82 MiB (raw: 42.10 MiB)

processed 1,420 files, 1.420 GiB in 0:04
snapshot 6b3c91af saved

Notice the deduplication efficiency: while the source payload is 1.420 GiB, only 14.82 MiB was encrypted and written to repository storage.

docs.title: Step 4: Stream Data Directly via STDIN (Database Dumps)
docs.text:
You can stream uncompressed database backups directly into Restic without staging raw unencrypted SQL dumps onto the local disk:

pg_dumpall -U postgres | restic backup \
  --stdin \
  --stdin-filename "postgres-full-cluster.sql" \
  --tag "database" \
  --tag "postgres"

docs.title: Step 5: Verify the Created Snapshot
docs.text:
List all snapshots associated with the target tag to confirm the snapshot was registered:

restic snapshots --tag "production"

Expected output:

ID        Time                 Host        Tags                 Paths
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6b3c91af  2026-11-03 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production,web-tier  /var/www/html, /etc/nginx
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 snapshot

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Verify Repository Integrity — Ensure newly written snapshots pass cryptographic checks.
  • Restore Data — Test disaster recovery procedures by restoring files.

docs.title: How to Initialize an Encrypted Restic Repository
docs.text: Task

docs.title: Initialize an Encrypted Restic Repository
docs.text: This procedure guides you through creating and provisioning a new encrypted Restic backup repository. You can initialize repositories on local filesystems, Amazon S3, MinIO object storage, or SFTP endpoints.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before beginning this procedure, ensure you have:

  • Restic CLI v0.16.0 or higher installed on your client machine.
  • Write permissions on the destination local path or administrative credentials for your remote object storage.
  • A strong repository password (minimum 16 characters recommended) stored securely in your secrets manager.

docs.title: Step 1: Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
To avoid retyping credentials and target repository locations in subsequent commands, export the primary environment variables in your active shell or systemd service file:

Local StorageAmazon S3 / MinIOSFTP Remote Server 
export RESTIC_REPOSITORY="/mnt/backups/restic-repo"
export RESTIC_PASSWORD="YourSuperSecurePassword123!"

export RESTIC_REPOSITORY="s3:https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/company-cold-storage/restic"
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"
export RESTIC_PASSWORD="YourSuperSecurePassword123!"

export RESTIC_REPOSITORY="sftp:backup-user@backup.internal.lan:/srv/restic"
export RESTIC_PASSWORD="YourSuperSecurePassword123!"

docs.title: Step 2: Execute Repository Initialization
docs.text:
Run the restic init command with the modern repository version 2 format (default in Restic v0.14+ for compression support):

restic init

docs.title: Command Execution Output
docs.text:
created restic repository 82ef1a364b at /mnt/backups/restic-repo

Please note that knowledge of your password is required to access
the repository. Losing your password means that your data is
irrecoverably lost.

[!CAUTION] If you lose your repository password, data recovery is mathematically impossible. Always store the password in a password manager or corporate vault (such as HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager).

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the Repository Initialization
docs.text:
Confirm that Restic can read, decrypt, and parse the newly generated configuration and keys:

restic check

Expected output:

using temporary cache in /tmp/restic-check-cache
enter password for repository:
repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
created new cache in /home/operator/.cache/restic
load indexes
check all packs
check snapshots, trees and blobs
no errors were found

docs.title: Step 4: Add a Secondary Recovery Key (Recommended)
docs.text:
To protect against operator turnover or accidental credential loss, configure a secondary recovery key:

restic key add

Follow the interactive prompts:

enter password for repository: [Original Password]
enter new password: [Secondary Recovery Password]
confirm new password: [Secondary Recovery Password]
saved new key with ID b9c071a1d948

You can view active repository keys anytime:

restic key list

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Now that your repository is initialized, proceed to:

  • Create Backups — Schedule and execute your first snapshot.
  • Verify Repository Integrity — Set up automated repository consistency checks.

docs.title: How to Enforce Retention Policies and Prune Data
docs.text: Task

docs.title: Enforce Retention Policies & Prune Data
docs.text: This procedure explains how to apply retention policies to clean up old backup snapshots and physically reclaim disk space by pruning orphaned pack files.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Read and write permissions on the repository storage backend.
  • Exclusive access or scheduling outside active backup windows to prevent lock contention.

docs.title: Step 1: Preview Retention Policy with --dry-run
docs.text:
Never execute retention pruning without first previewing which snapshots will be preserved and which will be deleted:

restic forget \
  --keep-daily 7 \
  --keep-weekly 4 \
  --keep-monthly 12 \
  --dry-run

docs.title: Reviewing the Policy Evaluation Table
docs.text:
Restic prints an ASCII matrix illustrating its decision for every snapshot:

Applying Policy: keep the last 7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly snapshots
keep 3 snapshots:
ID        Time                 Host        Tags        Reasons
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
6b3c91af  2026-11-03 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production  daily snapshot
e49f012a  2026-11-02 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production  daily snapshot
9a12b3c4  2026-10-26 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production  weekly snapshot
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

remove 1 snapshots:
ID        Time                 Host        Tags        Reasons
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
3c8e19b0  2026-09-01 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production  
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

1 snapshots have been removed, run `prune` to reclaim space.

docs.title: Step 2: Apply the Retention Policy (forget)
docs.text:
Once the dry-run output matches your compliance requirements, execute the policy without --dry-run:

restic forget \
  --keep-daily 7 \
  --keep-weekly 4 \
  --keep-monthly 12

This dereferences expired snapshots. As explained in Retention & Pruning Lifecycle, this step deletes the snapshot descriptors but does not free raw disk space yet.

docs.title: Step 3: Physically Reclaim Storage (prune)
docs.text:
Run the prune command to garbage-collect orphaned blobs, repack fragmented pack files, and delete obsolete data:

restic prune

docs.title: Prune Summary Output
docs.text:
repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
loading indexes...
loading all snapshots...
finding data that is still in use for 3 snapshots
[0:06] 100.00%  3 / 3 snapshots
searching used packs...
collecting packs for repack and prune...
repacking packs:
[0:02] 100.00%  4 / 4 packs repacked
rebuilding index:
[0:01] 100.00%  1 / 1 indexes rebuilt
deleting obsolete index files:
[0:00] 100.00%  2 / 2 index files removed
removing 18 old packs...
[0:01] 100.00%  18 / 18 packs removed
done, reclaimed 4.821 GiB (78.4% of repository)

docs.title: Step 4: Combined Single-Step Maintenance Command
docs.text:
To streamline routine maintenance in scheduled cron jobs, combine both operations using the --prune flag:

restic forget \
  --keep-daily 7 \
  --keep-weekly 4 \
  --keep-monthly 12 \
  --prune

[!TIP] Run restic forget --prune during low-traffic maintenance windows. The prune phase requires an exclusive lock and temporary additional scratch bandwidth for repacking packs.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• CLI Command Cheat Sheet — Fast reference of retention flags.
  • Error Codes & Troubleshooting — What to do if prune fails due to lock timeouts.

docs.title: How to Restore Files and Mount Snapshots
docs.text: Task

docs.title: Restore Files & Mount Snapshots
docs.text: This procedure walks you through recovering data from a Restic repository. It covers snapshot identification, complete directory restores, granular single-file recovery, path filtering, and mounting snapshots as a virtual filesystem with FUSE.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Read access to the Restic repository.
  • Adequate free disk space on the target destination path to accommodate the uncompressed restored payload.
  • fuse3 package installed if using the virtual mount capability.

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the Target Snapshot
docs.text:
Query your repository to locate the snapshot containing the files you need to restore:

restic snapshots --path "/var/www/html"

Sample output:

ID        Time                 Host        Tags         Paths
----------------------------------------------------------------------
6b3c91af  2026-11-03 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production   /var/www/html
e49f012a  2026-11-02 10:45:00  web-prod-01  production   /var/www/html
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Note the snapshot ID (e.g., 6b3c91af or use the alias latest).

docs.title: Step 2: Inspect Snapshot Contents
docs.text:
Before initiating a restore, inspect the file tree within the snapshot:

restic ls 6b3c91af

To search for a specific filename within a snapshot:

restic find config.php --snapshot 6b3c91af

docs.title: Step 3: Perform a Complete Restore
docs.text:
Restore the entire contents of a snapshot into an isolated staging directory:

mkdir -p /mnt/restore-staging
restic restore 6b3c91af --target /mnt/restore-staging

Expected output:

repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
restoring <Snapshot 6b3c91af of [/var/www/html] at 2026-11-03 10:45:00.000 by operator@web-prod-01> to /mnt/restore-staging
summary: 1,420 files, 120 dirs, 1.420 GiB restored in 0:03

docs.title: Step 4: Selective Granular Restore (Single File or Directory)
docs.text:
When you only need a specific configuration file or subfolder, use the --include flag:

restic restore latest \
  --target /tmp/recovery \
  --include "/var/www/html/wp-config.php"

Verify that only the requested file was restored:

ls -la /tmp/recovery/var/www/html/wp-config.php

docs.title: Step 5: Mount Snapshots via FUSE (Interactive Browse)
docs.text:
On Linux and macOS, you can mount the entire repository as a read-only filesystem. This lets users browse historical snapshots using standard terminal tools (cd, cat, grep, cp):

  1. Create a local mount directory: 

    mkdir -p /mnt/restic-mount

  2. Mount the repository: 

    restic mount /mnt/restic-mount &

  3. Browse through point-in-time snapshots: 

    ls -la /mnt/restic-mount/snapshots/


total 0
dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov  3 10:45 2026-11-03T10:45:00+00:00
dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov  2 10:45 2026-11-02T10:45:00+00:00
lrwxr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov  3 10:45 latest -> 2026-11-03T10:45:00+00:00
  1. Unmount when finished: 
    fusermount -u /mnt/restic-mount

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Prune & Enforce Retention — Learn how to purge obsolete snapshots.
  • Error Codes & Troubleshooting — Resolve permissions and mount errors.

docs.title: How to Verify Repository Integrity and Detect Bit-Rot
docs.text: Task

docs.title: Verify Repository Integrity & Detect Bit-Rot
docs.text: This procedure details how to run systematic integrity checks against a Restic repository. Regular verification guarantees that indexes, pack headers, and encrypted data blobs are intact, catching storage media degradation and bit-rot before a critical disaster recovery restore is required.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Read access to the target repository.
  • Network bandwidth capacity proportional to the verification mode (standard metadata audit vs. full payload download).

docs.title: Verification Tiers
docs.text:
Restic offers two levels of verification:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Tier 1: Metadata Check
        T1["restic check"]
        T1 --> A1["Index validation"]
        T1 --> A2["Tree reference validation"]
        T1 --> A3["Pack file size validation"]
    end

    subgraph Tier 2: Deep Cryptographic Read
        T2["restic check --read-data"]
        T2 --> B1["Download every encrypted packfile"]
        T2 --> B2["Poly1305 MAC re-calculation"]
        T2 --> B3["SHA-256 payload checksum validation"]
    end

docs.title: Step 1: Run Standard Metadata Verification (Weekly)
docs.text:
The standard check scans index structures, snapshot pointers, and structural references without reading entire data payloads. This is lightweight and fast:

restic check

Expected output:

repository 82ef1a364b opened (version 2, compression level auto)
created new cache in /home/operator/.cache/restic
load indexes
check all packs
check snapshots, trees and blobs
[0:12] 100.00%  3,210 / 3,210 snapshots
no errors were found

If errors appear during index loading, proceed to the Troubleshooting Matrix.

docs.title: Step 2: Run Cryptographic Bit-Rot Audit (--read-data)
docs.text:
To detect silent storage media corruption (bit-rot), execute a full read-check. Restic downloads each pack file, decrypts it, and confirms that the SHA-256 hash matches the index entry:

restic check --read-data

docs.title: Proportional Subsetting (Monthly Maintenance)
docs.text:
For large multi-terabyte repositories where downloading 100% of the repository is cost-prohibitive, verify a 10% random sample monthly using --read-data-subset:

# Checks 1/10th of the repository packs (shard 1 of 10)
restic check --read-data-subset=1/10

Subsequent runs can check shard 2/10, 3/10, etc., achieving 100% repository coverage over 10 consecutive cycles without spikes in cloud egress fees.

docs.title: Step 3: Automate Verification with Exit Code Alerting
docs.text:
Integrate verification into your operational monitoring using this bash script wrapper:

/usr/local/bin/verify-restic.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

export RESTIC_REPOSITORY="/mnt/backups/restic-repo"
export RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE="/etc/restic/password.txt"

echo "[$(date -Is)] Starting Restic integrity audit..."

if output=$(restic check 2>&1); then
    echo "[$(date -Is)] SUCCESS: Repository integrity verified."
    exit 0
else
    echo "[$(date -Is)] CRITICAL: Integrity check failed!"
    echo "${output}"
    # Trigger alerting webhook (e.g., Slack / PagerDuty)
    curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
      --data "{\"text\":\"Restic repository integrity failed at $(hostname): ${output}\"}" \
      "${ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL}"
    exit 1
fi

Make the script executable and schedule it via cron or systemd timer:

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/verify-restic.sh

docs.text:
